sentences.text: Training for the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System shall be role based and shall cover normal coordination, constrained operations, recovery actions, and degraded system use.

The Regional Flow Manager shall receive advanced instruction on interpreting demand and capacity information, leading collaborative decisions, and authorizing operational measures in the Regional Flow Platform.
Air traffic controllers shall be trained to understand how flow measures, sequencing changes, and calculated times affect sector workload, runway demand, and controller tactical flexibility.
The Tower Supervisor shall receive practical training on the Tower Sequence Manager, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter.

Ramp personnel shall be trained under the direction of the Ramp Control Lead to use the Ramp Movement Board without substituting system indications for required visual checks, radio coordination, and local safety procedures.

The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative shall be trained to submit, review, and update Flight Intent Message data through approved interfaces and to assess the operational effect of Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time changes.

Ground handling personnel shall be trained by the Ground Handling Dispatcher on the Handling Resource Planner and on procedures for confirming that resource constraints are represented accurately before they influence collaborative decisions.

The Slot Coordinator shall receive training on the Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, and applicable Business Rules Registry entries so that slot actions are applied consistently and transparently.

The Network Operations Liaison and Airspace Sector Planner shall be trained to coordinate regional constraints, sector load conditions, and network measures using the Sector Load Monitor and Common Situation Display.

The Airport Duty Manager shall be trained to recognize when an Airport Capacity Plan requires revision and when the operational state should move from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall be trained to explain weather uncertainty in operational terms and to verify that the Weather Ingest Gateway supports the assumptions used during briefings.

The Emergency Response Coordinator shall participate in recurrent training so that emergency priorities are integrated into flow management decisions without obscuring command authority or safety responsibilities.
The Deicing Coordinator shall receive seasonal refresher training on how deicing capacity assumptions are represented in demand and departure metering tools.
The Data Governance Steward shall train operational users on data quality responsibilities, privacy expectations, and the correct interpretation of audit records in the Audit Event Ledger.
The System Support Engineer shall train superusers on service status checks, access fault escalation, and safe use of the Contingency Operations Console during partial outages.

Initial training shall include classroom instruction, supervised workstation practice, scenario walkthroughs in the Digital Briefing Room, and observed operational shadowing before independent system use is authorized.
Recurrent training shall be required at least annually and after major changes to the Regional Flow Platform, Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, or Flight Data Exchange.

Simulation exercises shall use realistic traffic samples, weather constraints, surface congestion, airline schedule pressure, handling resource shortages, and recovery objectives to test coordinated decision making.

Each exercise shall include participants from tower, ramp, airline operations, handling, airport operations, network coordination, meteorology, data governance, and system support functions when those functions are relevant to the scenario.
Exercises shall cover transitions among Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, and Slot Compliance State.

Simulation events shall require users to compare automated recommendations with local knowledge, document significant decisions in the Collaborative Decision Log, and explain departures from system proposals.
Human factors safeguards shall include workload monitoring, clear alert prioritization, consistent terminology, confirmation steps for high impact actions, and protection against silent mode changes.

Workstation layouts shall support rapid comparison between the Common Situation Display, Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, and relevant advisory messages without forcing users to copy critical values manually.

Training assessments shall verify that users can identify stale data, time synchronization problems, duplicate flights, conflicting constraints, and inappropriate automation reliance before such issues affect live operations.

Post-exercise reviews shall use evidence from the Performance Analytics Warehouse and Audit Event Ledger to improve procedures, refine training materials, and confirm that human performance concerns are assigned to accountable owners.
